facts.raw_span: 20-year history of progressive ataxia
8-month history of 'spasms' in his throat
difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Hypometric saccades
Truncal and limb ataxia
Decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate
Bradykinesia and mild rigidity
Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz
Patient was unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of the palatal musculature
No clicking was noted by patient or examiners
Results of testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 were normal
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

concepts.why: The patient's 20-year history of progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with spinocerebellar ataxia.
The patient's palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz and inability to stop it with voluntary use of the palatal musculature are characteristic of palatal myoclonus.
The patient's progressive ataxia, difficulty with gait, and bradykinesia and mild rigidity are consistent with multisystem atrophy.
The patient's cerebellar ataxia and palatal myoclonus are consistent with cerebellar ataxia with myoclonus.
The patient's hypometric saccades, bradykinesia and mild rigidity, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with progressive supranuclear palsy.
The patient's progressive ataxia, decreased vibratory sense, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with corticobasal degeneration.
The patient's cerebellar ataxia, palatal myoclonus, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy.
The patient's progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with ataxia-telangiectasia.
It explains the normal results of testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12, suggesting the possibility of another type of spinocerebellar ataxia.
